evidence_notes: jmrozanec__cron-utils::CVE-2021-41269: Source side confirmed — CronParser.parse included raw cron expression in IllegalArgumentException, and the fix commit cfd2880f80e62ea74b92fa83474c2aabdb9899da removed it. EL payload tests (${...} Runtime.exec-style) are present in the patch. However, no evidence shows the exception message reaches an EL-capable interpolation sink in a vulnerable deployment.
traex_judge_gl_mech_0040_initial: Prior judge correctly split this case away from Bean Validation because no buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate or equivalent EL interpolation sink was demonstrated.

The ledger row correctly identifies the evidence gap. Before promoting, source-review the downstream consumption path: trace whether the IllegalArgumentException from CronParser.parse is caught and its message interpolated through an EL-capable context (validation layer, logging framework with expression evaluation, template engine, or UI rendering).
main_issue: The mechanism is conceptually coherent but the sink half is entirely hypothetical. The patch only proves that raw attacker input was removed from an error message; there is no source-reviewed evidence that the resulting exception message reaches an EL-capable interpolation sink (e.g., buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate, JEXL, or a UI template engine). Without confirming the downstream sink, the boundary cannot be promoted or used for reliable recall.
mechanism_name: parser error message carrying attacker expression text into downstream interpolation risk
suggested_guideline: Parser error message downstream EL risk: attacker-controlled parser input is copied into an exception or error message containing EL payload syntax, and that message is later consumed by an EL-capable interpolation or rendering layer. The confirmed source shape is CronParser.parse including the raw cron expression in an IllegalArgumentException message. The sink shape (e.g., buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate, JEXL interpolation, or template rendering) must be source-reviewed and confirmed in at least one deployable code path before this boundary can be promoted.

evidence_notes: CVE-2022-46166 fix commit c14c3ec12533f71f84de9ce3ce5ceb7991975f75 shows the exact API replacement: StandardEvaluationContext + MapAccessor → SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors(DataBindingPropertyAccessor.forReadOnlyAccess(), new MapAccessor()).withRootObject(root).build() across DingTalk, Discord, Hipchat, and LetsChat notifiers.
The boundary is correctly kept separate from Bean Validation message interpolation and Jinjava property resolution — those have different sinks and fix semantics.
Future cases with similar SpEL evaluation-context selection (e.g., other Spring projects using StandardEvaluationContext for untrusted expressions) would strengthen coverage.
main_issue: Single-case coverage is inherently limited, but the mechanism is narrow, specific, and internally coherent. The evidence is solid: a concrete fix commit replacing StandardEvaluationContext with SimpleEvaluationContext across multiple notifier paths. The boundary text names specific classes, APIs, and guard conditions, making it highly retrievable and actionable.

evidence_notes: ballcat_projects__ballcat_codegen::CVE-2022-24881: source-to-sink trace confirmed — GeneratorServiceImpl.generatorCode obtains templateFile.getContent() and passes to templateEngineDelegator.render(), with both Velocity.evaluate() and FreeMarker Template.process() sinks consuming the untrusted content directly.

ballcat_projects__ballcat_codegen::CVE-2022-24881: fix commit 84a7cb38 confirms missing guard — adds FreeMarker TemplateClassResolver.SAFER_RESOLVER and Velocity SecureUberspector, precisely matching the claimed safe-fix semantics.

Boundary scope is correctly narrow: reviewer notes explicitly exclude Bean Validation message interpolation, SpEL notifier template evaluation, and Jinjava sandbox-bypass as distinct mechanisms with different sources/sinks/fixes.
main_issue: Solid mechanism-level boundary: source shape (editable template content loaded as string), sink shape (FreeMarker/Velocity render with unrestricted features), missing guard (no SAFER_RESOLVER/SecureUberspector), and safe fix (add engine sandbox before render) are tightly aligned. Only one representative case, but the evidence is thorough with source, sink, and fix-commit confirmation.
mechanism_name: untrusted template text evaluated by template engine

main_issue: The three cases share a tight mechanism: Jinjava template expressions reach the same resolver (JinjavaBeanELResolver) and tag property access paths, each bypassing a different facet of the same sandbox — missing restricted class (CVE-2020-12668), missing restricted base object (CVE-2025-59340), missing restricted method/package + direct bean read bypass (CVE-2026-25526). The fix family is consistent (extend restriction sets, add guard checks, route through sandbox-aware resolution). The boundary is well-scoped to Jinjava-specific sandbox escape without over-generalizing to broader template injection.
mechanism_name: Jinjava sandbox bypass through incomplete property or method restrictions

evidence_notes: dropwizard::CVE-2020-11002: ViolationCollector.addViolation passes msg directly to buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate; fix adds InterpolationHelper.escapeMessageParameter and escapeExpressions.
dropwizard::CVE-2020-5245: Fix adds ESCAPE_PATTERN for ${ and escapeEl before buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate.

browserup-proxy::CVE-2020-26282: LongPositiveConstraint.isValid interpolates attacker value into errorMessage then calls buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate; fix adds MessageSanitizer.escape for backslash, braces, and dollar signs.
main_issue: All three representative cases share the same sink (buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate with EL-capable interpolation), the same source shape (attacker-controlled values or message fragments containing EL syntax), the same missing guard (no metacharacter escaping before template construction), and convergent fix semantics (escape ${, {, }, $, backslash or use message-parameter APIs). The boundary correctly excludes non-Bean-Validation sinks and parser-error cases.
mechanism_name: Bean Validation message template EL interpolation injection
